question: Sea level rises about 1 cm per hectopascal of pressure drop. An eye reads 910 hPa, the air outside 1,010. Pressure-driven surge, in metres?
move: Before blaming one force, work out how much of the effect it can carry.
trap: Crediting the low pressure with most of a surge several metres high.
hint: Work out how far the eye sits below the surrounding pressure.
source: Pugh, Tides, Surges and Mean Sea-Level
reference: Pugh, Tides, Surges and Mean Sea-Level, John Wiley & Sons, 1987
